summary.text: A 54-year-old man sustained a right proximal tibial fracture in a traffic accident at age 11, underwent two ORIF procedures at a local hospital and later implant removal, but a residual varus deformity and gait disturbance persisted. He had worked at construction sites, was a former smoker, and his history was notable only for an appendectomy. Right knee pain gradually worsened in recent years, leading to referral.

Examination showed an antalgic gait, right knee flexion of 130 degrees and extension of -15 degrees, and negative McMurray, Watson-Jones, Lachman and pivot-shift tests. Radiographs showed a femorotibial angle of 188 degrees, MPTA 68 degrees, CDI 0.84 and a radiographic SMD of 84.3 cm on the right versus 87.5 cm on the left. CT showed bony union of the prior fracture, and MRI suggested a medial meniscus posterior root tear.

Planning aimed for an MPTA of 88 degrees, and simulation led to OWDTO being selected over HCWHTO. Under general anesthesia with femoral nerve block, arthroscopy identified a type II MMPRT, repaired with suture anchors using the all-inside technique with meniscus centralization. A 20 degree curved osteotomy with a 25-mm gap was filled with autologous iliac crest graft and granular beta-TCP and fixed with a medial plate, an anteromedial small plate and an extra screw, followed by immobilization and staged rehabilitation.

Radiographs at one month showed MPTA 88 degrees, CDI 0.83 and slope 8 degrees. At two months the weight-bearing line ratio was 59.0% and radiographic SMD 86.5 cm, leaving about 1 cm discrepancy. CT at one month showed a type I hinge fracture, with no correction loss observed during follow-up, and CT at seven months showed progressive bone healing. At five months knee flexion was 140 degrees with full extension. At 12 months he was pain-free and had returned to work.

figures.caption_summary: Figure 10 Preoperative simulation comparing open-wedge distal tuberosity tibial osteotomy (OWDTO) and hybrid closed-wedge high tibial osteotomy (HCWHTO) for prediction of postoperative spina–malleolar distance (SMD).A: Hybrid closed-wedge high tibial osteotomy (HCWHTO). The osteotomy was initiated approximately 40 mm distal to the lateral tibial cortex and extended medially to approximately 15 mm distal to the joint line. The hinge point (H) was defined near the joint surface at the medial one-third of the line connecting the lateral starting point and the medial endpoint. A simulated 20° correction around the hinge point displaced the medial malleolus from its pre-correction position (M) to the post-correction position (M′), resulting in a predicted postoperative SMD of 83.9 cm. The anterior superior iliac spine is indicated as (S).B: Open-wedge distal tuberosity tibial osteotomy (OWDTO). The osteotomy was initiated approximately 35 mm distal to the medial tibial joint line and directed toward the tip of the fibular head, with the hinge point (H) set 5 mm medial to the lateral tibial cortex. A simulated 20° correction around the hinge point displaced the medial malleolus from (M) to (M′), resulting in a predicted postoperative SMD of 86.5 cm. The anterior superior iliac spine is indicated as (S).In both simulations, postoperative SMD was calculated as the linear distance between the anterior superior iliac spine (S) and the medial malleolus after correction (M′).
figures.attribution_notes: Index-patient preoperative simulation; referenced in b00026. Simulated values, not a performed procedure for HCWHTO.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the ten JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.
Preoperative leg length discrepancy appears as approximately 30 mm and as 32 mm; clinical SMDs (80/83 cm) and radiographic SMDs (84.3/87.5 cm) are kept as separate measurements.
CDI is called unchanged postoperatively while printed values are 0.84 and 0.83; author wording and values are both retained.
Laterality of the osteotomy is not stated in the operative text; it is taken from the Figure 8 caption, which places the open wedge site in the right knee.
Discussion statements about literature, general technique advantages and author causal interpretations are not recorded as patient facts.
Follow-up times differ across statements (final follow-up at five months, CT at seven months, pain-free at 12 months) and are kept at their own stated times.
